newsitem.title: BRAZIL: AT&T plans new Brazil, LatAm branches in '97.
newsitem.headline: AT&T plans new Brazil, LatAm branches in '97.

text.p: American Telephone & Telegraph (AT&T) plans to open a third branch in Brazil to expand business communications services and open offices in Bolivia and Peru in 1997, AT&T officials said.
Wilson Otero, managing director of AT&T Brasil Ltda, said the firm expects to a open third Brazilian branch in the country's south in late 1997 to serve firms operating in that region.
"The potential as a result of the economic opening in Brazil is great," Otero told reporters during a conference.
The U.S-based telecom giant also plans in 1997's third quarter to open branches offering business communications services in Bolivia and Peru to serve growing markets in the two Andean countries.
"This shows our commitment to the region," said Lorraine Levy, AT&T marketing and sales manager for Latin America and the Caribbean.
AT&T has 28 in-country offices among the region's 50 nations, offering global communications services to firms with overseas offices.
In Brazil, it has branches in Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo, and the new branch may be opened in Florianopolis or Curitiba, he added.

Apart from the host of voice and data services it now offers, AT&T in Brazil also plans to launch next year an Internet service similar to its WorldNet program begun in the U.S. last year, Otero said.
"We're hoping to enter the corporate Internet market to offer a domestic solution," he said.
The firm now offers a gateway giving clients access to the Internet, company officials said.

AT&T also hopes to become an operator in the promising Brazilian telecom market. The company is part of a consortium that aims to bid in the coming weeks on concessions to operate in the B Band cellular frequency.
